proposed.explanation:
Profit attributable to CIB's (COMI) own shareholders was 82,238,852,000 EGP for the year ended 31 Dec 2025, up from 55,196,394,000 EGP in 2024 – an increase of roughly 27.0 billion EGP, or about 49 % year-on-year. The growth was underpinned by net interest income rising from 91,064,222,000 EGP to 107,699,631,000 EGP over the same period, indicating a healthy core-earning engine.

For your 7-year bank-income goal, this trajectory is encouraging: a large, profitable bank with nearly 50 % profit growth in a single year suggests a solid dividend-paying base. You already hold 250 shares (≈ 32,000 EGP at 128 EGP), which is about 61 % of your 52,000 EGP portfolio. Because that concentration already exceeds the 50 % single-stock cap, buying more COMI with your 20,000 EGP cash would push the position even further over the limit, so I recommend simply holding your existing 250 shares for now. If you wish to add to the position later, you would first need to diversify into another name to bring COMI below half the portfolio.

Risks and uncertainty: the figures are from a single fiscal-year condensed report; one strong year does not guarantee the next. Interest-rate shifts, credit-quality deterioration, or regulatory changes could compress net interest margins or raise provisions. Your medium loss tolerance means you should monitor quarterly results and the bank's dividend policy over the coming years rather than assuming the 49 % growth rate will repeat. This is guidance, not a guarantee of returns.
